title.narrative: Output 7.5. Increased capacity of Member States to develop fair and effective labour migration frameworks, institutions and services to protect migrant workers

description.narrative: By August 2023, the National Employment Authority (NEA), a department of the Ministry of Labour and Social Protection, had established two new Migrant Resource Centres (MRCs) in Mombasa and Eldoret, bringing the total number of MRCs established in 2022/2023 biennium to four (4): 3 established by NEA and one established by Central Organization of Trade Unions Kenya (COTU-K), in June 2023. All four MRCs are operational by August 2023 at NEA / Labour Offices as well as at COTU HQ. i.e. 2 in Nairobi ; 1 in Mombasa ; 1 in Eldoret. The MRCs have strengthened and expanded the Kenya's capacity to offer relevant support services for migrant workers before travel overseas and upon return, including dispute resolution where migrant workers are in a dispute with their employers or recruitment agencies. Other services include legal referral support for migrant workers seeking access to justice, business registration processes for returnees, psychosocial support and psychological counselling, financial advice, and support for re-integration of returnee migrant workers, including supporting families of migrant workers to trace migrant workers they have lost contact with. Over the period from January 2022 to June 2023, more than 2,000 persons, actual or potential (job seekers) migrant workers in need of various types of support, were served by the two MRCs in Nairobi. With support from the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation, the ILO supported the Government of Kenya through NEA to establish three (3) Migrant Workers Resource Centers (MRCs) that are housed in premises of the implementing partners i.e. the National Employment Authority. The ILO also supported the carrying out of four feasibility assessments, which informed the development of an operational plan for the MRCs. With support from the United Kingdom [Foreign Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO)], the ILO provided support to the Central Organization for Trade Unions to establish an MRC at their premises in Nairobi.

description.narrative: In July 2022, the Government of Kenya, in consultation with the social partners, increased its minimum wage rates with an effective date of 1 May 2022, as gazetted in the Kenya Gazette Supplement No.114, published on 1 July 2022. The decision was made following the recommendations of the two tripartite wages councils, namely the General Wages Council and the Wages Council for Agriculture. Because Kenya has a system of multiple sectoral rates, with different rates by region and occupation, these adjustments led to an increase in about 155 different minimum wage rates. The previous round of minimum wage rates adjustments dated back to 2018. The ILO supported the consultations on minimum wage adjustments in both the General Wages Council and the Wages Council for Agriculture. The ILO, with the support of the Government of the United States, provided support to the Ministry of Labour to facilitate the consultations that took place in the two councils in April 2022. It also provided the technical inputs during these meetings. Specifically, the two Wages Councils consultations were held on 11 and 12 May 2022, for the Agricultural Wages Council and on 13-14 April 2022 for the General Wages Council meeting. The Agricultural Wages Council formulates recommendations on the monthly and daily rates for 10 different occupations, while the General Wages Council makes recommendations on monthly, daily, and hourly rates for 15 different occupational groups. Previous to these contributions, the ILO also supported a review of wages policies in Kenya, including on minimum wage fixing, collective bargaining and public sector wages in Kenya.

description.narrative: In November 2022, the Kenyan Central Organization of Trade Unions (COTU-K) and the National Federation of Worker and Employee Trade Unions in Lebanon (FENASOL) signed an inter-union Memorandum of Understanding (MOU), to ensure a more solid protection framework for Kenyan workers travelling to (and returning from) Lebanon. The MOU is framed in the context of Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work, engages the unions to advocate for ratification of relevant Conventions and has a monitoring and review mechanism and at least three technical virtual meetings have been held between the two union federations in 2023 The ILO contributed to the development and implementation of the MOU by supporting and facilitating a mission to Lebanon in July 2022 by COTU-K. The mission included meeting with dozens of Kenyan domestic workers to hear their challenges and concerns and close discussions with FENASOL. These exchanges led the trade union federations to affirm their mutual support to work individually and at a corridor level to protect workers. The ILO continues to engage periodically with both federations to support ongoing implementation of the MOU.

description.narrative: On 8 August 2023, The Cabinet of the Government of Kenya approved Kenya National Labour Migration Policy, which has been developed in consultation with social partners and informed by the international labour standards and other instruments, aligning with the regional and national labour migration frameworks. This Policy sets out to protect the human and labour rights of migrant workers, and protect migrant workers in Kenya. The government commits to undertake gap analysis on and ratify relevant ILO standards relating to private employment agencies, domestic workers and forced labour framework now puts Kenya in a good position to be able to legislate the Labour Migration Management Bill. The Policy adoption also demonstrates the commitment of the government to assist in the better regulatory mechanisms and realignment of the mandates of the government agencies and other relevant stakeholders on their roles and responsibilities under labour migration governance in Kenya With support from the Government of Switzerland, the ILO delivered technical support to inform the Labour Migration Policy as well as the Labour Migration Management Bill and the Migrant Workers Welfare Fund. In 2022, ILO technical support was availed to the review of the draft of the policy and the bill. The ILO also continues to be engaged in the development of the Kenya Migrant Worker Welfare Fund, a key Policy priority captured in both the Policy Implementation Matrix as well as the Labour Migration Management Bill. The ILO took part and technically supported the multi-Agency technical Committee on the development of regulations for the Kenya Migrant Workers Welfare Fund. This work on the development of the Kenya Migrant Welfare Fund is supported by both the Government of Switzerland and the United Kingdom.
